title: Design: can two epics run concurrently on one repo?
description:
Operator question (2026-08-20): does the architecture support parallel cloud orchestrators on the same repo — multiple epics at once — including their Telegram interactions?

TODAY THE ANSWER IS NO, deliberately. The RunRoom dispatch lease is one per PROJECT (idFromName(project)), not per epic, so a second submission is refused naming the holder (--queue parks it instead). That follows D4: exactly one .tick/ writer per project, because two orchestrators mutating tick state would corrupt it.

That is right for TRACKER WRITES and wrong as a general limit: a factory that can only ever run one epic at a time is a serial machine. The question is whether the exclusive thing can be narrowed from "the project" to "the tracker mutation", and it needs designing rather than assuming.

What to establish:
1. WHAT ACTUALLY CONFLICTS. Tick state is per-tick JSON files with a field-level merge driver, and each epic touches a disjoint set — so two epics writing different ticks may not conflict at all. activity.jsonl is append-only. The real contention is probably narrower than the whole tracker: concurrent commits to the same run branch, and any two runs both claiming the SAME tick.
2. LEASE GRANULARITY. Options: keep project-exclusive (today); lease per epic with a narrow tracker-write lease serialising only the commit; or lease per epic with each run on its own tick-run/<epic> branch, merging at closeout as they already do. The third looks closest to how git already handles this.
3. GIT CONTENTION. Two runs pushing tick-run branches is fine; two runs merging to the default branch at closeout is not necessarily. Say what serialises.
4. TELEGRAM, which the operator asked about specifically. Gates already carry run/tick/epic identity and are answered by id via inline keyboards, so BUTTON answers are unambiguous across concurrent epics. FREE-TEXT answers are not: the rules recorded on hdt (reply-to scopes it; bare text with exactly one open question resolves it; two or more must REFUSE and list) were written for one run and must hold for N. Topics-per-project does not disambiguate two epics in the SAME project — consider whether the unit of a topic should be the epic rather than the project.
5. RESOURCE LIMITS. Concurrent epics multiply containers and spend. Whatever the answer, per-project concurrency needs a cap and it belongs with the dispatcher policy, not in a prompt.

Deliverable is a design decision with a recommendation, not an implementation: say what becomes possible, what stays serialised and why, and what it costs. If the answer is "stay serial for now", say that explicitly with the reason, so it is a decision rather than an omission.
notes: 2026-08-21 16:55 - Seam (wave 2, six wide). Design only — you own docs/design and the tick you may file. Do not change code. Relevant new fact: kji just made the dispatch lease's sibling, the wave-width slot, enforceable per epic; two epics on one repo have to reason about BOTH that and D4's one .tick/ writer per project.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision covering lease granularity, what genuinely conflicts in .tick/ and git, how Telegram disambiguates across concurrent epics, and a concurrency cap; the design doc updated; and either an implementation plan as follow-up ticks or an explicit recorded decision to stay serial with its reasoning.
